- Pin Node 26.13.0, pnpm 12.14.0, TypeScript 7.0.2, and exact dependency versions with a real lockfile.
- Add Oxfmt, type-aware Oxlint, and strict TypeScript checks, including exact optional properties and unchecked indexed access.

Verified locally on commit `004f542` (the unchanged content was tested before committing):

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm verify`: passed.
- The actual commit passed both installed Git hooks; `pnpm check:commits --from origin/main --to HEAD` also passed.

- `verify` currently checks tooling configuration, formatting, lint, and types. Add meaningful tests and include them in verification with the first application implementation.

Add local Git-history inspection for the deterministic release pipeline, independently of PR #2.

- Reject shallow/incomplete history, missing or malformed tags, and tags that do not resolve to commits with explicit error codes.
- Use argument arrays, bounded Git processes, disabled replacement refs/lazy fetching, and isolation from inherited Git repository-routing environment variables.

## Summary

Post-merge Quality runs fail because strict Commitlint treats GitHub's generated `Merge pull request #…` messages as ordinary conventional messages. Formatting, lint, types, and tests already pass. Reproduced the failure from [the latest main run](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/42409078822) locally.

- Select non-merge commits using Git's actual parent-count filter and validate each with the same Commitlint policy used by the commit hook. Keep merged side-branch commits in the check; do not use first-parent traversal or message-pattern exemptions.
- Avoid Commitlint's `--git-log-args=--no-merges`: the pinned version silently ignores that filter, as confirmed by regression testing and its Git-client implementation.
- Enforce unscoped commit subjects (`feat: …`, `fix: …`, `refactor: …`) and scoped PR titles (`feat(exports): …`, `fix(ci): …`, `refactor(release-context): …`). Keep the existing conventional type list.
- Share a base syntax configuration while preserving the release metadata parser's existing acceptance of scoped and unscoped conventional messages.
- Document the policies and cover real merge graphs, invalid side-branch commits, merge-looking ordinary commits, empty ranges, invalid refs, shallow history, hooks, and title/message format differences.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: Fix post-merge CI validation and distinguish commit and PR title formats.
impact: Generated merge commits no longer fail CI; ordinary commits remain strict and PR titles identify their feature or component.
required_action: Use unscoped conventional commit subjects and scoped conventional PR titles. Remove the scope from the final commit subject when squash merging.
```

## Verification

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` — passed.
- `pnpm verify` — formatting, type-aware lint, TypeScript, and all 151 tests passed.
- Rechecked the exact historical ranges `4d67734..b63849e` and `3533e6d..4d67734` with `pnpm check:commit-range` — passed, while the original checks reject the generated merge messages.

- Scoped commits and unscoped PR titles now fail contribution checks. When squash merging, edit the default scoped PR-title subject to the unscoped commit form.
